title: University of Manchester Plans Major New Centre for Education, Research and Innovation in Bengaluru
summary: The centre will offer students internships, work placements and industry projects, building on the university's ties with Indian institutions and companies.
body_html:
Bengaluru, 15 October 2026: The University of Manchester has announced plans to set up a major new centre in Bengaluru, giving it a permanent base in India for collaboration with students, researchers, industry and alumni.

The centre will build on the university's Partner-Enabled Learning model, which places real projects with employers, public bodies and community organisations inside degree programmes. Students will gain practical experience through internships, work placements, micro-internships and industry-led projects.

The university said Bengaluru was chosen for its position as one of India's leading hubs for higher education, technology and innovation. It already works with companies in India including Reliance, Tata and Infosys, and the centre will build on these links.

The announcement was made during the first Great North Mayoral Mission to India, held from 12 to 16 October 2026, at an event at Science Gallery Bengaluru attended by the Mayor of Greater Manchester, Bev Craig.

"Our new Centre will be at the heart of deepening those relationships and I'm very excited to see what we can give, and what we can learn over the coming years," said Professor Duncan Ivison, President and Vice-Chancellor of The University of Manchester.

The university already has international centres in Dubai, Hong Kong, Shanghai and Singapore. In India it runs a dual-award PhD with IIT Kharagpur, launched in 2021, and works with institutions including the Indian Institute of Science, BITS Pilani, the Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research and the Manipal Academy of Higher Education.
